newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Qinqi to offer B shares in first half.
newsitem.headline: Qinqi to offer B shares in first half.

text.p: Jinan Qinqi Motorcycle Co Ltd expects to launch an offer of 200 million B shares in the first half of 1997 and list them in Shanghai, a company spokesman said on Wednesday.
The company is among the 33 domestic enterprises named on Wednesday by the Securities Commission of the State Council as candidates for B share listing.
Haitong Securities Co Ltd would be the offer's domestic chief underwriter, with Yamaichi International (H.K.) Ltd the international coordinator, the official said.
The pricing and precise timing of the issue are not yet set, he added.
Qinqi, one of China's five largest motorcycle makers, plans to use the proceeds to revamp production facilities and import equipment for making motorbike parts, the official said.
Qinqi forecast output of one to 1.2 million motorcycles for 1997, compared with about 900,000 in 1996 and 700,000 a year earlier, he said.
About 90 percent of Qinqi's products were sold within mainland China in 1996, with the remainder exported, mainly to Southeast Asia and Europe, the official said.

The firm reported after-tax profits of 120.38 million yuan for 1995 against 108.72 million yuan in 1994. Its 1996 interim net surged to 80.19 million yuan over the year-earlier period's level of 40.39 million.

As of June 30 1996, Qinqi's share capital totalled 248.64 million shares, composed of 156.80 million state shares, 14.84 million legal person shares and 77 million A shares, according to its interim report.
The firm implemented a three-for-10 scrip payout in July 1996 as dividend for 1995 and a 2.3-for-10 rights offer last September.
